doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: 1950 European tour with Benny Goodman's sextet
summary: At 23 Hyman toured Europe with Goodman's sextet, with Zoot Sims, Roy Eldridge, Toots Thielemans and others; some broadcasts were recorded.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What was it like playing with some of the jazz legends? I mean is there one or two people that stood out in your mind from all the people you’ve played with over the years. I know you’ve played with Dizzy, and —

Well Benny Goodman certainly. Back in 1950, I got tapped to play with his sextet on a European tour. I was 23. And now that I think of it, Benny wasn’t any more than in his 40’s at that time, and we thought of him as the grand old man.
He’d already had his whole swing thing.

Yeah. We went to Europe with a group that included Zoot Sims and Roy Eldridge and Toots Thielemans joined us. He wasn’t yet an American, he was still living in Belgium. Charlie Short, the English bass player, the singer Nancy Reed, who am I leaving out? That’s about it. It was a wonderful thing. Some of those performances were recorded, too, I have tapes of some of them that were recorded for a radio program in Sweden and one or two others I guess that were somewhere else on the tour. We played Sweden and Switzerland, Italy, France.
